past.company_description: Fetch.ai is a decentralized network built to power autonomous AI agents that can discover, connect, collaborate, and transact with other agents seamlessly. The Fetch.ai ecosystem enables developers and users alike to build intelligent, self-operating systems that interact across the digital and real world.At the core of the platform are three integrated products:ASI:One: A family of agentic LLMs that interact with agents from Agentverse to expand their capabilities and perform real-world reasoning. ASI:One includes models like asi1-mini for fast, operational tasks and asi1-extended for deeper, complex reasoning. These models communicate via multi-agent protocols and scale by invoking services from the broader agent network.Agentverse: A developer platform designed for full control and extensibility. Built on the uAgents framework, Agentverse allows developers to create, host, and register agents that are interoperable across the Fetch.ai ecosystem. It provides built-in support for agent-to-agent messaging, payments, discovery, and deep ASI:One integration.Flockx: A no-code agent studio that lets users create personal or business agents without writing code. Flockx offers consumer-facing simplicity, and includes a professional Workbench for small businesses and teams looking to operationalize agent-based workflows. Agents created via Flockx are automatically indexed by ASI:One and published to Agentverse.Together, these components form a composable AI layer where intelligent agents can operate autonomously, reason with large models, and plug into business workflows, decentralized apps, and real-world systems.

past.company_description: Aspiring Scholars Directed Research Program (ASDRP) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit summer program that provides opportunities for high school students throughout the Bay Area, especially those who are underrepresented in STEM or who are socioeconomically disadvantaged, to conduct high-level novel scientific research. Students participate in research projects across various subjects in STEM, including chemistry, biology, computational modeling, computer science, and much more.ASDRP provides students with research mentors and over $200,000 worth of research equipment in our research laboratory. Students are matched with research mentors who have experience in academia or industry in their particular field; together, they design a research project. These projects are not science experiments in which the results are known a priori, but rather are original research projects that expand current scientific knowledge. Students execute research projects, learn scientific reading and writing skills, write research papers on their results, undergo mock peer-review, publish their research papers in the ASDRP Communications online journal, and give poster presentations at the end-of-summer expo. We follow up with students from ASDRP to help place them into university research laboratories and industry internships in subsequent summers. The inaugural cohort of ASDRP started in summer 2018.Please see fremontstem.org/asdrp for details.
